title: Pain au Levain (Sourdough Bread)
steps: LEVAIN BUILD: Combine 130g bread flour, 9g rye, 85g water, 28g stiff culture. Cover and ripen at 21°C for 12 hours.
AUTOLYSE: Mix 731g bread flour + 37g rye with 505g water until shaggy. Cover, rest 20–60 min.
MIXING: Sprinkle 17g salt over dough. Add levain in fist-sized chunks. Mix on speed 2 for 1½–2 min. Target dough temp: 24°C.
BULK FERMENTATION: Ferment covered for 2½ hours.
FOLDING: Fold twice — at 50 min and 100 min.
SHAPING: Divide into 2 × ~680g. Pre-shape, rest 20 min, then shape round or oval. Place seam-up in floured bannetons.
BAKING: 225°C with steam, 40–45 min, until deep russet brown. Cool fully on rack.
tips: A stiff levain (60% hydration) gives this bread its French character: open crumb, russet crust, and delicate flavour. Bake the same day — retarding overnight dulls the subtle notes. 95% bread flour + 5% rye is the classic formula; the rye feeds the levain and adds colour.
